court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: IV Additional Family Court at Chennai, O.P. No.704 of 2018
facts_of_case: The parties are Vishwanath and Srichandrika Ravindranatha Sharma. The husband filed a petition under Section 13(1)(ia)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act seeking decree for dissolution of marriage. The wife moved an interim application under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act seeking maintenance. The trial court allowed the application and directed the husband to pay Rs.25,000/- per month each to his wife and minor child.

legal_principles.principle: The court should not mechanically entertain and allow an application without considering vital aspects.
legal_principles.held: hereby, the appellant has brought this appeal on the ground that the IV Additional Family Court, Chennai ought not to have mechanically entertained and allowed the Interim Application filed under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, without considering various vital aspects raised by the appellant.

legal_principles.principle: A court should not pass an order that a party cannot comply with.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, the impugned order passed by the Family Court to pay Rs.25,000/- per month each to the wife and the minor child is virtually unenforceable as the appellant has been paying house rent allowance, transport allowance, utility allowance and in addition thereto he has been undertaking flight expenses from Dubai to Chennai for the sake of proceedings pending before this Court.

outcome.final_order: The final order is that the appeal against the fair and decretal order dated 27.11.2019 passed by the IV Additional Family Court, Chennai is dismissed.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
